gap: Same 3 options but 100 variants (`MAX_VARIANTS` in `src/lib/product-input.ts`), so large matrices do not fit; the editor offers every combination of option values but has no matrix grid for thousands of rows.
criteria: A product saves with up to 2,048 variants over at most 3 options; the 2,049th is refused with a plain message (unit test on `productInput`).

The product editor edits a 2,048-variant matrix without freezing (paged or virtualised grid, bulk fill of price, stock and SKU per option value) and saves it in one transaction within a stated time budget (integration test).
Cart, listing, search, JSON-LD and stock reads still answer for a 2,048-variant product without a query per variant (integration test).
The storefront variant picker stays usable for a large matrix (option dropdowns, unavailable combinations marked).

feature: Product data fields (SKU, barcode, weight, cost, HS code, origin)

shopify.text: Native. Per product or variant: SKU (unique), barcode (up to 20 per product or variant), weight (physical products, used for shipping rates), cost per item (optional; gives projected profit and margin), HS code and country/region of origin (physical products; origin when customs information is on).

criteria: SKU is unique per store (a duplicate is refused with the SKU named).
GTIN is 8 to 14 digits, weight is a positive whole number of grams, HS code is 6 to 10 digits and origin is a two-letter country; anything else is refused with a plain message.
HS code, origin and weight belong to shipped variants only: a download keeps none (`products.ts` writes null for non-physical).
A variant's cost is typed like a price in the store's main currency, may stay empty, and is copied to the order line when sold so later changes never rewrite history (D152).

gap: Staff put products into nested categories and flat tags by hand (`product_terms`) and shoppers browse, filter and sort them, but a term is only a name, a slug, a parent and a position (`commerce.terms`): no description or picture of its own (SEO title and description and the names' translation came with D168, row `catalogue.seo-fields-title-description-handle-sitemap-hreflang`), and no manual order of products inside one (`product_terms` has no position; sorts are featured, newest, price, title). A description or picture is possible only through a custom field on the term bound to a block (D119). Rated Full in the first report; re-rated Partial because collection content, SEO and manual ordering are what a merchant uses a collection for.
criteria: A category or tag has its own description and picture, kept per language, shown on its page and in its metadata (e2e). Its SEO title and description are counted once, in `catalogue.seo-fields-title-description-handle-sitemap-hreflang` (D168).
Category and tag names are translatable per language and appear in the store translation worklist (integration test).
Products can be put in a manual order inside a category or tag, and a 'manual' sort follows it on the listing (integration test).
Still holds: staff assign products to nested categories and tags, menus link to them, and the listing filters and sorts (existing tests).

history.why: Read the schema and storefront: a category or tag is a name, slug, parent and position; no own description, picture, SEO text, translation or manual product order. Staff can still group products by hand, so Partial, not Missing.

gap: No rules fill a category or tag; terms are set by hand (verified: `product_terms` is the only membership, no rule table); shopper filters (D78) are applied per request, not saved as a collection.
criteria: An owner defines a collection by rules (product category, tag, price range, availability, manufacturer, variant option, a public custom field) joined by all or any, with a live preview count.
Membership follows product changes (price, stock, tags, status) without anyone re-running it, and unpublished or archived products are never members (integration test).
A rule collection can be a category or tag page, a menu link and a content grid source, like a manual one.
Rules are checked per store: a rule cannot read another store's data (integration test).

gap: Only campaigns (D114): percentage off, 'buy N pay for M' and a free product over an amount, applied to ordinary products. There is no bundle product with components, no fixed bundle price and no stock tied to its parts (verified: no bundle table or kind in `src/db/schema.ts`).
criteria: A bundle is a product made of components (variants with quantities) with a fixed or computed price; its stock is the lowest sellable amount of its components.
Placing an order reserves each component's stock and records the components on the order line; a return or refund puts the right components back (integration test).
`cartSummary()` and `placeOrder()` agree on a bundle's price, VAT and discounts, in a euro scenario too (`checkout-kinds.int.test.ts`).
A bundle with a sold-out component shows as unavailable instead of overselling.
Delivery is chosen per variant (shipped, downloaded or a booked service); a download variant on sale needs a file, and keeps no stock, weight or manufacturer.
The shopper's consent to an immediate start is recorded before a download is bought.
A paid order gets download links from a private bucket that stop at the product's download limit and expiry (`order_downloads`).
A file belongs to its store: another store's file is refused, and a removed file stays for earlier buyers.

gap: Built and held by tests (wave 3, D172, in production since 6 October 2026): a variant keeps selling at zero (`product_variants.stock_policy = 'continue'`, physical goods only, `backorder_days` 1 to 90 required, database checks); only such a variant's level may go below zero (trigger `inventory_levels_rules`); the product page and the phone's bar say 'On backorder' with the days and keep the button, the cart accepts up to 20 a line, the cart, slide-out cart, checkout, order page, My account and the confirmation email say how many units are on backorder and within how many days, `order_lines.backorder_quantity`/`backorder_days` are kept, structured data says `BackOrder`, a gift or weekly box is never backordered, and `commerce.draw_order_stock()` keeps each live checkout's physical claim whatever the order of payment, so what a shopper read before paying is what the order says. Held by `e2e/backorder.spec.ts` (5 tests: Norwegian, Swedish and Danish page, cart, phone drawer, JSON-LD, a normal variant still sold out), run by me on a production build of the final tree and all passed, PGlite rules, `backorder.int.test.ts`, a krone and a euro scenario in `checkout-kinds.int.test.ts`, and the unchanged test `refuses more than is in stock`. Stays Partial, bucket D, for what no test can settle: the delivery-time sentences ('expected to ship within N days', hand-written in nb, sv, da and en, never machine-translated: `HAND_WRITTEN_ONLY`) are consumer legal text nobody has read, and a reviewer found they may not state what Directive 2011/83/EU Art. 6(1)(g) and Art. 18 ask (the time by which the trader undertakes to deliver; the 30 days run to delivery, not dispatch); the wording was left as written for a lawyer (docs/wave-3-inventory.md section 8, item 6), as was the 7 days of transport the editor's reminder assumes. A person must read them before this row is Full. Also not done: the WordPress plugin was not updated, so a site on it shows a backorder variant as sold out (the API serves it as `out` with `backorder_days`); product cards in listings state no backorder; the setting is per variant (the editor has one switch that sets all of a product's variants).
criteria: A variant can be set to keep selling at zero stock; the cart then accepts any quantity for it and the product page says it is on backorder (e2e).

An order for such a variant is placed and its lines are marked backordered (`order_lines.backorder_quantity` and `backorder_days`: what the shopper was told at placement, settled at payment, where for a live hold it can only go down); stock may go below zero only for flagged variants (database rule and integration test).
Variants not flagged still refuse more than is in stock and write nothing (existing test `refuses more than is in stock`).
Inventory analytics and the admin handle negative stock (days of stock, alerts) and `checkout-kinds.int.test.ts` has a scenario.

history.why: Wave 3 run 1 (docs/wave-3-inventory.md, D172 proposed, tree not committed). Read the migrations (stock_policy and backorder_days checks, the negative-stock trigger, draw_order_stock() as replaced by 20261006121317), cart.ts, checkout.ts, the product page, cart, order and email surfaces and the tests; ran the unit files, the integration files (backorder, backorder-email, review-money-inventory, checkout, checkout-kinds incl. the krone and euro backorder scenarios, analytics-inventory-backorder) and e2e/backorder.spec.ts (5 passed) on a fresh database and a production build of the final tree. All four criteria hold in the running product, but the delivery-time sentences are unreviewed consumer legal text that a reviewer found may not state the delivery time the cited law asks for, so the row is held at Partial (bucket D) until a person has read them.

gap: No pre-order mode, release date or back-in-stock list (verified: no such table, column or route). Shopify itself offers pre-orders only through apps, so this is stretch.
criteria: A variant can be a pre-order with a release date and optional deposit or pay-now rule; cards, product page, cart and the order say so (e2e).
Pre-order orders are flagged, kept apart from shippable stock, and listed for the owner by expected date (integration test).

A shopper can ask to be told when an out-of-stock variant is back: consent recorded, one email when stock is added, unsubscribe link, no email to a typed-in address of another person (integration test).
`cartSummary()` and `placeOrder()` agree for a pre-order, euro included.

gap: The product gallery takes pictures only, 12 at most (`MAX_MEDIA`, `product_media` has a url, thumbnail and alt). Video reaches a product page through a 'Video' custom field (YouTube or Vimeo embed, D119) or a video block in a product layout; there is no 3D model support and no uploaded video in the gallery.
criteria: The gallery takes pictures and videos (uploaded, with a poster, or YouTube and Vimeo) in an order the owner sets, and shows them in that order on the product page (e2e).
A 3D model (glTF or GLB) can be added to a product and is viewable in the gallery with a picture fallback for browsers without support.
Every media item has alt or description text per language, and the library lists where each is used (D88).
The media limit and the file size limits are stated in the editor and enforced on the server (unit test).

shopify.text: Native. Metafields extend products, variants, customers, orders and collections with custom data; the help page states no plan limit.

criteria: An owner defines groups of typed fields (23 types: text, number, measurement, money, link, relation, file, video, group, repeater, flexible content and more) and places them on products, variants, categories and tags, pages, articles, the store, customers and orders.
Values are kept per language where the type is text, checked on the server against the groups the finished thing gets, and are private until the owner makes them public.
Public values are shown by layouts, blocks and bindings, usable as listing filters and in search, and never rendered as HTML.
Customer and order fields are never readable on the shopper's side (a test lists the modules that may read `field_values`).

gap: Repeaters, flexible content and relation fields exist (D119, D120), so structured data can sit inside a thing; there are no standalone entries of a defined type with their own admin list, publishing state and public pages or templates.
criteria: An owner defines a content type (fields) and creates entries of it in a list of their own, with draft and published states and per-language texts.
An entry can be referenced from fields and builder blocks and drawn by a content grid or its own page template.
Entries are per store, included in the store translation worklist, and in store copies per `COPY_RULES` (test).
An entry's public page is in the sitemap only when published.

feature: SEO fields: title, description, handle, sitemap, hreflang
criteria: Changing a product, category, tag or page address creates a permanent redirect from the old one automatically; manual redirects collapse chains and refuse loops (integration test).
Owners add, edit, import and export redirects, and see a 404 report of what shoppers and crawlers asked for (integration test).
Categories and tags carry their own SEO title and description per language, used in their page title, description, Open Graph tags, hreflang alternates and the sitemap (integration test, e2e).
The sitemap lists only live addresses with hreflang alternates and never a redirected one (existing sitemap tests extended).

history.why: D168 (wave 2, second run, docs/wave-2-redirects.md). Criteria 1 and 3 reworded as the spec's section 6.4 says: automatic redirects point at the thing and cannot chain, so chains and loops concern manual redirects; '(see collections)' dropped, so the SEO text is counted here and not in catalogue.collections-manual. Read the code and ran the cited tests on a fresh database (unit and PGlite 2183 tests, integration 128 tests, e2e redirects, terms and smoke on a production build 28 passed). (1) Address changes leave automatic redirects for products, categories and tags (commerce.redirects triggers; PGlite and redirect-resolve.int.test.ts), pages and articles keep page_redirects (commerce.test.ts, renamed twice); manual redirects store a chain as its final destination and refuse a loop in the service, the import plan and the database trigger (redirects.int.test.ts, redirects.test.ts), and a chain formed later is followed in one response up to ten hops (redirect-resolve.int.test.ts). (2) The manager, CSV import and export and the 404 report are the ones rated on storefront.url-redirect-manager. (3) terms.seo holds a title and description per language, saved through updateTerm(), shown by termMetadata() as the title, description, Open Graph and X tags and hreflang alternates with the term's own canonical, never another language's text, copied by clone_store() and duplicate_store(), listed in the translation worklist (scope terms); e2e/terms.spec.ts checks the Swedish page against the Norwegian one. (4) storeSitemap() lists category and tag pages with live products per market with alternates and x-default, leaves empty ones out and lists no old address after a product or category rename (seo.int.test.ts, extended by this step with a product renamed twice) and e2e/smoke.spec.ts checks a category entry with hreflang. Caveats: the signed-in term editor's search section is held by a renderToString test and the integration tests, not an end-to-end test; the sitemap's no-old-address check after a rename is an integration test, and the e2e smoke test does not rename anything.

criteria: Export writes every product and variant to CSV (handle, translations, options, SKU, GTIN, prices per market, stock, cost, HS code, origin, media addresses, categories, tags) as a job for large stores.

Import reads a Shopify-format and Kaizen-format file with a dry run that lists each row's problem, then creates or updates by handle and SKU through `saveProduct()` and `commerce.set_price`, resumable after a failure (integration test).
Export then import round-trips a product without change (integration test); cells are escaped against spreadsheet formula injection.
Every import is per store with a size limit and an audit entry; archived variants are switched off, never deleted.

history.why: Wave 2, first run (D165 proposed, docs/wave-2-data.md; working tree not yet committed, migrations not yet applied). Read the code and ran in a fresh database: csv, csv-writers, product-csv, product-csv-shopify, product-import, product-import-writers, data-job and db/data-jobs unit and PGlite tests (356 tests with the others of the run), and product-export, product-import, product-roundtrip, data-jobs, data-permissions, money-review int tests (277 integration tests over 14 files, all passed). Criterion 1: a store over the direct limit becomes a job in parts in the exports bucket; the export of every column of the contract is held by product-csv.test.ts. Criterion 2: a Kaizen and a Shopify file (current and older names, Shopify header names read from its published template, fixtures made up) get a dry run with a code per row problem, then apply product by product through getProductForEdit() and saveProduct() (a scan test holds that no import code writes products, variants, prices or stock itself); a run killed after N products is taken up again with no product doubled; the export and import routes are called as handlers with the member's guard. Criterion 3: export then import changes nothing (no price row, no updated_at), and the injection canary round-trips. Criterion 4: limits, store isolation, one active import, an audit entry per job with counts and no cell; archived variants are switched off, never deleted. The review's two high findings (clock-change days of the order range belongs to the order export; stale stock written by an import after a picture fetch) are fixed and have regression tests. Caveats, not blockers: the Shopify reader is held to Shopify's published template and docs, not to every file a store can produce; the storage adapter (signed upload, list, signed download) was run only against a fake and has never run against Supabase Storage; the import and its job page have view and route tests but no signed-in browser run (no admin fixture, D158); parsePrice() of the editor reads a price cell like 12.345 as 12345 whole units (a Kaizen file always writes two decimals, Shopify's too).

shopify.text: Native. The bulk editor changes many products and variants in a table (a column per property such as price, SKU, compare-at price; a row per item), and also collections, customers and metafields; variant inventory is bulk edited from the Inventory page. The help page states no item limit or plan restriction and recommends CSV import for large volumes.

gap: Built and held below the screen, not through it. The server side is complete and tested: previewBulk/startBulk/continueBulk for status, archive, unarchive, categories and tags, price (percentage half up, or amount per market) and stock, applyGrid/previewGrid/undoBatch with conflicts, 500/50 limits, one products.bulk_edited entry per batch and failures with reasons, all through getProductForEdit() and saveProduct() so commerce.set_price keeps the price history (src/server/bulk-edit.int.test.ts, src/lib/bulk-edit.test.ts, passed). What the criteria name is the merchant's screen: tick boxes in the products list, one confirmation step, a grid with a preview of changed cells and an undo. That state machine (src/components/admin/products-bulk.tsx, products-grid.tsx, bulk-recent.tsx) is held only by renderToString view tests (src/components/admin/bulk-views.test.ts, which render the states but never click), and the e2e the spec named for criterion 1 (tick two rows, Change price, confirm) was not written: e2e/data-export.spec.ts only holds that a visitor without a session gets nothing, because the repo has no signed-in admin fixture (D158). The server actions in products/bulk/actions.ts are thin wrappers that cannot be called outside Next's request context, so they are untested too. Also unbuilt by design: the products list is not paged until wave 3, so 'select all matching' and 'select the page' choose the same rows.
criteria: The product list selects many products and applies a bulk action (status, archive, add or remove categories and tags, price change by percentage or amount, stock set) in one confirmed step.
A grid edits price, SKU, stock and cost across variants in a table with a preview and undo; every change goes through the same validation as the editor and `commerce.set_price` (integration test).
A bulk change is limited per request, runs per store, writes one audit entry per batch, and reports which items failed and why.

history.why: Wave 2, first run (docs/wave-2-data.md; working tree not yet committed). Read src/server/bulk-edit.ts, src/lib/bulk-edit.ts, the three bulk components and products/bulk/actions.ts and ran bulk-edit.test.ts, bulk-admin.test.ts, bulk-views.test.ts and bulk-edit.int.test.ts (all passed): every action and the grid go through saveProduct() and commerce.set_price, limits, conflicts, undo as its own batch and one audit entry per batch hold. Held at Partial, not Full, because the criteria are the merchant's screen (select many, one confirmed step, a grid with preview and undo) and nothing drives that screen: the view tests only render states, the e2e the spec named was not written (no signed-in admin fixture, D158), and the server actions are untested. The first signed-in browser test of the list and the grid would make this Full.

shopify.text: Native. Tracking is switched on per product or variant (Inventory section, "Track quantity"). Inventory states: on hand is every unit at a location and is the sum of committed, unavailable and available; committed is set aside and cannot be sold (an unfulfilled order, a draft order reservation, a transfer ready to ship); available is what can be sold; unavailable (damaged, quality control, safety stock) and incoming are the other states.

gap: Built and tested (wave 3, D172, in production since 6 October 2026): every change of `inventory_levels.on_hand` is an append-only `inventory_movements` row written by a trigger (reason, source, account, order, return; `inventory_ledger_check()` proves the movements add up to the level and still does after the 24-month clean-up, which keeps each level's newest movement), an Inventory page with on hand, committed to checkouts in progress, available and owed per variant and location, adjust with a reason (Set to or Adjust by, reviewed, a stale row is a conflict), a history page, stock files as D165 jobs with a dry run (`inventory_import`, `inventory_export`), a per-variant low-stock level that sends the owners one digest email per crossing (`stock_alerts`, `sendLowStockNotices()`), negative stock in the analytics and the control center, and the AI manager's `stock_levels`, `stock_history`, `set_stock` with location and reason. Why it stays Partial: (1) no signed-in screen has been clicked: there is no signed-in admin fixture (D158), so the Inventory table, the review list, the history page, the stock-file pages and the product editor's stock rules are held by `renderToString` tests and by integration tests of the server functions the actions call (`adjustStock()`, `inventoryPage()`, `stockHistory()`), not by the screen a merchant uses (D165's bulk editor stayed Partial for the same reason); (2) the stock export has no `on_hand_was` column, so a file counted from an export has no conflict check unless the person adds that column; (3) a variant created with stock already at or under its level sends no first email until it recovers and crosses again; (4) the history page and the pending crossings are not load-tested at 100,000 movements; (5) `src/server/inventory-perf.int.test.ts` (the C4 guard) is not reliable: its 20-line `placeOrder()` timed out at 60 s in most of my runs against a database that already held an earlier perf store or ran other test files at the same time (probably stale planner statistics; the statement caught running for minutes was `orderLineRows()`'s cart-line read in `src/server/checkout.ts`, unchanged by this wave apart from two columns) and passed in 7 s alone on a fresh database, as in the Gates run; the cause is not found. Not matching Shopify: no unavailable or incoming states, no transfers or purchase orders (`catalogue.inventory-transfers-and-purchase-orders`), no untracked variants; 'committed' is the live checkout holds only, because a paid order has already drawn its units here.
criteria: An inventory page lists variants per location with on hand, committed to checkouts in progress, and available, and staff adjust a level with a reason (received, damaged, correction, recount).
Every change to a level, from an adjustment, sale, cancellation, refund or return, is an append-only history row with who, when, reason and the order (integration test).
Stock can be updated in bulk from the page (reviewed before it is saved) and from a file with a dry run.
A variant crosses its low-stock level once: the owners get one email per run listing each crossing once, never one per sale (integration test).

shopify.text: Native. Inventory transfers move stock between locations or to and from external locations, created from Products > Transfers (draft, ready to ship, in progress, transferred, cancelled) with bulk CSV import, receiving per line, and purchase orders linked to transfers.

gap: No transfers and no purchase orders: no transfer or purchase order table or screen (verified); Kaizen has stock locations with a rank and a history of every stock change (wave 3, D172) but nothing moves stock between them. One row for the one Shopify feature (it replaces orders.inventory-transfers).
criteria: Staff create a transfer between two locations; sending reduces the origin and shows incoming stock at the destination, receiving adds it (partial receipt supported, integration test).
A purchase order to a supplier lists variants, quantities and cost, is received in parts, and updates stock and variant cost history without rewriting earlier orders' cost.
Both write to the inventory history with their reference.
A cancelled transfer returns committed stock to the origin, and a transfer never takes a location below zero (integration test).
A product has up to five purchase options (intervals) charged by Stripe Billing on the store's own account, with free trial, sign-up fee and commitment.
Subscribers pause, skip and change their subscription themselves and are reminded before a charge.
Weekly subscription boxes (D102) become orders through `placeOrder()` at the cutoff and are charged when sent.
A variant has a price per market in the country's own currency, VAT-inclusive, changed only through `commerce.set_price` (history kept; an empty price means not sold there).

A shopper can see amounts in another currency the store offers, converted at the store's rate and rounded to its step; amounts are written to the database in the country's own currency (euro scenario in `checkout-kinds.int.test.ts`).
Advertised reductions use the 30-day reference from `commerce.current_prices` (Omnibus).
Not covered and not claimed: percentage price adjustments per market; prices are set per market, conversion applies only for the shopper's chosen currency.

gap: Companies with a customer group, invited employees, a company number filled in at checkout and a group discount (D108, D63) exist (`customer_companies` has name, tier, employee share, member cap). No company locations, no buyer roles beyond owner and employee, no order approvals and no PO number at checkout (verified in `src/db/schema.ts`). Net payment terms are the row checkout.b2b-payment-terms (wave 4) and are not counted here.
criteria: A company has several locations (billing and shipping addresses), and a buyer is assigned to locations and a role.
An order over a company-set limit waits for an approver before payment (integration test).
A buyer's PO number is asked at checkout and kept on the order and its documents (integration test, euro scenario).

shopify.text: Native, on every plan. Companies, company locations, net payment terms, quantity rules and quantity price breaks are on Basic, Grow, Advanced and Plus; Basic, Grow and Advanced allow 3 active B2B market catalogs, Plus unlimited; direct company catalogs and deposit, partial and per-fulfillment payment requests are Plus only.

gap: One whole percentage per customer group, off what is bought once (`customer_tiers.percent`, `memberLineOff()`); no price lists with their own prices, no per-group product visibility, no wholesale price per variant (verified). The umbrella row platform.b2b-companies-catalogs-terms is removed: its four parts are this row (price lists), catalogue.b2b-company-accounts (companies, locations, PO number), checkout.b2b-payment-terms (net terms) and catalogue.volume-pricing-and-quantity-rules (quantity rules and breaks).
criteria: A price list holds its own prices (fixed or a percentage on the market price) per currency and is assigned to a customer group or company; the shopper sees and pays it when signed in (integration test).
A catalogue limits which products or categories a group sees; a hidden product is not in listings, search, sitemap or recommendations for others, and a direct link answers not found.
`cartSummary()` and `placeOrder()` agree on list prices with VAT, in a euro scenario (`checkout-kinds.int.test.ts`).

gap: No quantity breaks, minimums, maximums or increments (verified: the cart only caps to stock and `MAX_LINE_QUANTITY`); 'buy N pay for M' campaigns (D114) are the nearest thing.
criteria: A variant (or price list) has quantity breaks (from N units, price or percentage) and the product page shows them.
A variant can have a minimum, maximum and increment per order; the cart refuses and explains a quantity that breaks them (integration test).
`cartSummary()` and `placeOrder()` agree on tier prices, euro included.

shopify.text: Native in the sense of Shopify's own free Search & Discovery app: related and complementary product recommendations on product pages. (The app is installed from the App Store.)

criteria: A product grid with a recommend source shows a cached stand-in for everyone and the browser swaps in the shopper's own, without cookies or AI needed.
Candidates come only from the store's data and pass `recommendable()`; anchors, the cart, purchased products and never-with rules are excluded (unit and integration tests).
AI only re-orders ids from that list, kept in the search cache, under the owner's cap, never for the held-out arm; its result is judged on tabs, not impressions.
Category and tag pages are page roles so recommendations work around them (D140).

shopify.text: Native in the sense of the free Search & Discovery app: filters shoppers refine a collection or search by, and sorting. (The app is installed from the App Store.)

criteria: Products, category, tag and search pages take sort and filters from the address (kinds, categories, tags, variant options, price range, public custom fields) and show matching facets.
Prices are compared as shown (without VAT for businesses, in the shown currency).
The unfiltered grid stays prerendered and the dialog follows each choice live on listing pages.

shopify.text: Native in the sense of the free Search & Discovery app: autocomplete, instant search, typo tolerance, multi-language support. (The app is installed from the App Store.)

criteria: Search stems per language (plural and definite forms find the singular), finds misspellings and parts of compound words by trigram similarity, and suggests as the shopper types.
Search by meaning is merged by reciprocal rank fusion and falls back to keywords when the model is unavailable.
A search that holds filters ('lampe under 500 kr') is read into filters by the model, cleaned in code; the model never names products or prices.

shopify.text: Native, as the free Shopify-built Search & Discovery app: synonym groups and product boosts (up to 10 search terms per boost), filters, and control of result types and out-of-stock visibility.

gap: `/admin/{store}/search` shows counts, zero-result queries and meaning help only (verified, `src/app/admin/(gated)/[store]/search/page.tsx`); no synonym, boost, bury or pin controls and none in `src/server/search.ts`. Listing filters and sorting (D78) are other rows. One row for the one Shopify feature (it replaces ai.search-merchandising, which was rated partial for filters only).
criteria: An owner defines synonym groups per language (one-way and two-way) and keyword search uses them (integration test).
An owner boosts, buries or pins products or categories, for all searches or for a query, and the result order follows it (integration test).
A zero-result query in the report offers to add a synonym or a redirect to a page.
Merchandising applies within the search cache's key (a change shows without stale results), is per store (store id on every query) and is copied by the store-copy rules (`COPY_RULES`).

shopify.text: Native in the sense of the free Search & Discovery app: analytics on the store's search and discovery performance. (The app is installed from the App Store.)

criteria: Every page search is logged (kept 90 days) with its result count and, when a result is opened, the click and its position.
The owner sees searches, share that found nothing, the terms ranked with results and clicks, and the zero-result terms with when they last happened (store search page and Analytics, D152).
Revenue after a search is stated as not tracked rather than guessed.

feature: Product feeds to Google and other channels

shopify.text: Native, through the Google & YouTube sales channel (installed from the App Store, managed by Google): automatically syncs products and store information to Google Merchant Center; available only for certain countries and currencies; free Shopping listings for eligible US merchants.

gap: No feed route, no channel admin and no sync (verified: no feed or merchant route under `src/app`). Credit elsewhere is only GTIN data on variants and product JSON-LD (`structured-data.ts`) that Google can read from the page, which is not a feed. One row for the one Shopify feature: it replaces the two feed rows in the AI and Customers domains. Planned in `docs/plan.md` (Phase 4, channels).
criteria: A tokenised feed address per market and language serves published products in Google Merchant Center format (id, title, description, link, image link, GTIN, brand, price with VAT in the market's currency, availability from stock, shipping and tax by country, 30-day price reference), validated against Google's required attributes in a unit test.
A euro scenario proves the feed's price equals the storefront's `shown()` price.
Products that may not be advertised (restricted, unavailable, no price) are left out and the admin lists each with the missing attribute; custom label fields can be mapped.
Meta, TikTok and Pinterest catalogue formats come from the same normalised product list.
Price and stock changes show in the feed within its stated refresh time. Live only once the Merchant Center account is connected (bucket B).

history.why: First report's skeptic recheck: credit for GTIN data and product JSON-LD only; the recheck's own text said 'partial leaning missing'. Entry written in wave 0 from the first report, which did not log it.
No feed exists; JSON-LD is not a feed. Merged with ai.product-feed-to-merchant-center and customers.google-shopping-and-merchant-center-feed (same Shopify feature), both already rated missing

gap: No standard product category or attributes: nothing exists that Shopify's or Google's taxonomy would map to. Kaizen has its own categories and tags (D50) and a Stripe product tax code per product (`txcd_…`), which classifies for tax and is not a browse taxonomy; no standard category list with attributes, so nothing to map to channels.
criteria: A product can be given a category from a standard taxonomy (searchable picker, stable ids) kept apart from the store's own categories and from the tax code.
The category's attributes are offered as fields and as filters; values are checked against the category.
The standard category and attributes reach the feeds (see the feeds row); a model may only suggest a category, which staff accept.

history.why: Tax code is a tax classification, not a product taxonomy; no criterion met

criteria: In the product editor staff ask the store's text model to write or improve a description, write search texts, or translate from the main language; the suggestion is shown for staff to edit and copy in and is never written to the product directly.
The model gets the product's own words and never prices or stock; its copy passes `findClaims()` (generic green claims, urgency, best price, money, stock) before it can be used.
Without an AI connection the editor works and the feature says so; usage is metered for the store.

shopify.text: Plus. The Combined Listings app is available only on Plus and enterprise commerce plans.

gap: None: no way to show separate products as one listing with shared options (verified: variants live inside one product only).
criteria: Separate products can be grouped into one listing with a shared option (for example colour); the listing card and page link to each product.
Each product keeps its own stock, price, SEO address and reviews; the cart holds the chosen product.
Search and feeds list the products once, with the canonical pointing to the right address.
